anti_overlap: fd-orchestration-terminal-consistency (parent) owns pure transactional correctness of the terminal sequence -- fencing, idempotency, at-least-once, per-step checkpoint, compensating transactions, session-vs-goal cardinality -- TREATED AS A CONCURRENCY/CONSISTENCY PROBLEM over a subject whose social/witness status is not in question. This fused lens declines any finding whose defect is purely transactional (a race, a duplicate write, a missing checkpoint) with no stranded-subject, missing-separation, un-witnessed-conferral, or pollution consequence.

fd-liminal-rite-passage (parent) owns pure rite-validity -- three-phase order, separation-before-reincorporation, witnessed conferral, the interrupted rite, the stranded liminal being, liminal pollution and resolution rites -- TREATED AS A PASSAGE-STRUCTURE PROBLEM over a crossing ASSUMED to be atomic and single-writer. This fused lens declines any finding whose defect is purely ritual (a skipped phase, an un-witnessed status, a pollution) that does not depend on a transactional mechanism (retry, fencing, provisional-accept, concurrent writers, checkpoint, consumer-optionality) to arise.

fd-elicitation-ritual-design (sibling) owns whether the formation interview elicited the RIGHT goal (comparative-advantage information quality, one-question-at-a-time interview craft) -- this lens is indifferent to goal QUALITY and asks only whether the formation/close CROSSINGS are transactionally-and-ritually valid, whatever the goal's content.

fd-kernel-phase-migration (sibling) owns the mechanical correctness of the DefaultChain change and the sprint.md/lib-sprint.sh/clavain-cli three-way transition-ownership sequencing as a MIGRATION-ENGINEERING problem -- this lens touches strategized-collapse only where the migration strands in-flight runs as double-/no-status rite subjects, not where it is merely a chain-versioning or code-port question.

fd-waqf-perpetual-trust (sibling) owns ownerless-drift, succession-across-many-administrators, and perpetual trusteeship over long time horizons -- this lens reasons about the single crossing and its immediate interruption/concurrency window, not stewardship across many custodians over time.

By construction this lens cannot report a finding that only one parent frame would surface -- the intersection-only constraint is its failure mode when the transaction frame and the rite frame do not actually cross at a specific status crossing in the doc.
decision_lens: For each status crossing this redesign introduces (charter -> Goal mint on /goal invocation; run auto-attach to an active Goal; Goal -> discharge with reflect/compound/verify/successor terminal steps; strategized-phase collapse from DefaultChain for new runs while in-flight runs keep their chain; interphase retirement without losing the statusline witness; tracker subsume/supersede verdicts; /goal-met session signal vs Goal-entity close), ask BOTH questions at once: (1) TRANSACTION -- is the crossing fenced against a second concurrent writer, idempotent under retry, checkpointed per-step so an interrupted session resumes rather than restarts, and compensated if a provisional accept is later invalidated? (2) RITE -- is the old status cut before the new is conferred (separation before reincorporation), does the crossing complete all phases in order, is the new status durably witnessed by the kernel/beads/later-sessions, is any subject left stranded in the margin, and is there a resolution mechanism bound to clean up half-crossings? Report ONLY when a defect requires BOTH frames: name the transactional mechanism AND the rite-validity/stranded-subject/witness consequence, and show in intersection_justification that deleting either half collapses the finding into a single-parent concern.
focus: The cross-product of transactional-correctness and rite-validity: every status crossing in this redesign (free-text intent -> minted Goal entity, active Goal -> discharged/closed Goal, strategized-phase -> retired chain, live tracker -> subsumed/superseded, /goal-met session signal -> goal-level terminal state) examined as ONE object that must both (a) survive interruption, concurrency, retry, and late-verification-failure as a transaction, AND (b) confer a witnessed, ordered, non-polluting new status as a rite. The lens lives exactly where the mechanism that makes the crossing transactionally correct MANUFACTURES OR CONCEALS a stranded liminal subject the rite-frame calls lethal, OR where the mechanism that makes the crossing a valid witnessed rite has NO transactional guarantee (no fencing, no idempotency key, no compensating action, no per-step checkpoint) so the witness itself can be half-conferred, double-conferred, or silently reverted.
name: fd-fused-witnessed-transaction
persona: Apply the perspective of someone who has been both a saga-coordinator engineer and an initiation-society officiant, and cannot stop seeing both frames at once. Every state change is, to them, simultaneously a transaction (does it fence, is the step idempotent under replay, is there a checkpoint so a dying session resumes mid-sequence, is there a compensating action if async verification later fails?) AND a rite (was the old status cut before the new was conferred, did the crossing pass all three phases in order, is the new status durably witnessed by a community that will treat it as real, is any subject stranded betwixt-and-between, and is there a resolution-rite bound to detect and clean up half-crossings before they pollute the next candidate?). Their obsession is the collision: they know the engineer's favorite fixes (at-least-once retry, provisional-accept-then-verify-async, silent single-writer fencing, idempotent replay) each either CREATE an intermediate state or HIDE it from witnesses -- exactly the stranded liminal being the officiant fears -- and that the officiant's demands (witnessed, ordered, all-the-way-through, community-attested) are transactional serializability+durability+no-partial-commit demands that, left un-fenced and un-checkpointed, let the witness be double-conferred or silently reverted. They refuse a finding that only one frame surfaces: a pure concurrency/idempotency bug with no stranded-subject or witness-validity consequence belongs to the orchestration parent; a pure phase-order/witness/pollution bug over an assumed-atomic-and-single-writer crossing belongs to the rite parent. Their unique yield is the seam: a crossing that is transactionally correct yet leaves a subject socially stranded or un-witnessed, or a crossing that is ritually valid yet has no transactional guarantee protecting the witness.
review_areas: Idempotency-replay MANUFACTURES a double-status subject: the doc's own axiom is at-least-once execution of any multi-step terminal sequence. If the Goal-discharge terminal steps (verify-against-charter -> reflect+compound -> successor-proposal) are made safe by idempotent retry, does a replayed reincorporation confer the new status a SECOND time onto a subject already reincorporated -- or, worse, replay a reincorporation whose separation half already ran, producing a subject holding both the old (open) and new (closed) status at once? (Requires orchestration: at-least-once/idempotency is the retry mechanism. Requires rite: reincorporation-without-fresh-separation is the missing-separation double-status defect.)

Provisional-accept-then-async-verify STRANDS the subject in the liminal margin with no resolution rite: shape (a)'s two-layer close accepts /goal-met provisionally and verifies against the charter asynchronously; the orchestration parent demands a compensating transaction for late verification failure. But the rite frame asks what the SUBJECT's status IS during the verify window and after a compensating revert -- is the Goal a witnessed-closed entity that later un-closes (a silently-reverting conferral), leaving a being that later sessions and next-goal already treated as discharged? Is there a resolution rite bound to detect and re-strand-then-reconfer, or does the compensation just flip a bit while the community still holds the stale witness? (Requires orchestration: the async-verify + compensation shape. Requires rite: the compensated state is a polluting half-crossing with no resolution ceremony.)

Fencing/single-writer designation makes the crossing serializable but ERASES the witness, or the witnessed crossing has NO fence: the doc states sessions close far more often than the goals they belong to, so two sessions WILL attempt goal-close concurrently. If the fix is a silent fencing token on the close transaction, is the winning close still WITNESSED (durable Goal-entity state the kernel and later sessions attest to) or merely serialized in memory and lost when the session dies? Conversely, if the witnessed conferral is the Goal-entity write with no fencing token, can two sessions each perform a valid-looking witnessed reincorporation, double-minting or double-discharging the same Goal? (Requires orchestration: fencing vs. the concurrent-writer inevitability. Requires rite: whether the surviving crossing is a durably-witnessed status or a lost/duplicated one.)

Cardinality mismatch as a phase-skip: /goal-met is a session-scoped signal, Goal close is goal-scoped -- different cardinalities the orchestration parent says must be reconciled explicitly. In rite terms, collapsing them (shape b: /goal-met IS goal completion) confers the goal-level reincorporation from a session-level separation -- a phase-skip where the community-binding witness (Goal discharge) fires without the goal's own liminal margin ever being entered, so a goal spanning many runs is reincorporated on the strength of one session ending. (Requires orchestration: the N:1 session-to-goal cardinality reconciliation. Requires rite: firing reincorporation from the wrong-cardinality separation skips the goal's own passage.)

strategized-phase collapse: missing-separation on the in-flight cohort: Decision 5 collapses strategized from DefaultChain for NEW runs while in-flight runs keep their chain (per-run --phases). The orchestration parent sees an unversioned chain migration with two concurrent chain definitions; the rite parent sees runs that were separated from the old chain but whose reincorporation into the new goal-formation-head chain is only conferred on new runs -- are in-flight runs left holding a retired phase-status the kernel no longer witnesses, stranded between a chain that no longer exists and one they were never cut into? Is there a resolution rite (a bound migration ceremony) or do they drift as polluting ambiguous runs contaminating the next chain read? (Requires orchestration: the concurrent-chain-definition migration with no fencing between cohorts. Requires rite: the in-flight cohort as stranded double-/no-status subjects with no resolution ceremony.)

interphase retirement: the witness outlives the authority, or the authority dies un-witnessed: interphase is a second parallel bead-scoped phase system that ships the statusline UX people see daily. Retiring its phase-authority (a rite: cutting the old status) while preserving its display surface (the witness) means the community keeps attesting to a status the retired authority no longer confers -- a witnessed-but-hollow status. The orchestration frame asks whether the retirement is atomic across the two phase systems or leaves a window where the kernel chain and interphase disagree on the run's phase; the rite frame asks whether the daily-visible statusline witness now attests to a status that has been separated-from but not validly reincorporated. (Requires orchestration: the two-system atomic-cutover/consistency window. Requires rite: a durable community witness that survives the authority it attested to.)

successor-proposal as an optional consumer of a mandatory rite: the doctrine is 'never leave a finished goal without a proposed successor' (mandatory), but shape (c) makes it a registered, individually-optional consumer of an unordered goal-close event. The orchestration parent's axiom: an optional consumer is not an enforcement mechanism. The rite parent: a reincorporation is only complete when its final witnessed step fires -- if successor-proposal is the terminal witnessed step and it is optional/best-effort, the Goal is discharged (old status cut) but the passage's final phase never binds, stranding the just-closed goal in a margin where the doctrine's successor-attestation never becomes real. (Requires orchestration: optional-consumer-is-not-enforcement. Requires rite: an un-fired terminal phase leaves the reincorporation incomplete and the successor un-witnessed.)

No per-step checkpoint means an interrupted terminal rite cannot resume its remaining phases: the orchestration parent wants a per-step checkpoint on the Goal entity (not a single closed/open bit); the rite parent's central hazard is the interrupted rite between the first and last mutation. Crossed: if a session dies after verify-against-charter and reflect but before compound and successor-proposal, does the Goal entity record WHICH phases of the discharge rite completed, so the next session resumes the remaining phases -- or does it hold a single open/closed bit that either re-runs the whole sequence (double-witnessing the early phases) or marks the goal closed with an unfinished rite? (Requires orchestration: per-step checkpoint vs. single-bit state. Requires rite: mid-threshold interruption strands the subject unless the completed phases are individually witnessed.)

severity_examples.condition: flag if the goal-close/discharge path defines no fencing token, lease, or single-writer designation AND the Goal-entity close is treated as the durable community witness, with no resolution mechanism to detect and collapse a double-conferred discharge
severity_examples.intersection_justification: Orchestration alone flags the missing fence as a concurrency bug (two writers, no serialization) but, treating close as a bit-flip, sees at worst a duplicate write to be de-duplicated. Rite alone flags double-reincorporation as a pollution defect but assumes a single officiant per crossing and cannot see that the redesign structurally invites two, because it does not reason about concurrent writers. Only the intersection sees that the un-fenced transaction IS the mechanism that produces two valid-looking witnessed rites for one subject, and that the missing resolution ceremony is what lets the double-witness pollute the next formation. Delete the orchestration half and there is one officiant, no double; delete the rite half and it is a mere duplicate write with no polluting-successor consequence.
severity_examples.scenario: Two sessions both belonging to the same active Goal reach a terminal condition near-simultaneously (the doc explicitly says sessions close far more often than goals). Both fire the Goal-discharge sequence. There is no fencing token or single-writer designation on goal-close (orchestration defect), so both perform a valid-looking witnessed reincorporation: two Goal-entity close writes, two reflect artifacts, two successor proposals. The Goal is now double-discharged -- a subject reincorporated twice, and because next-goal's ranked-candidate machinery consumes the successor proposal, TWO successor goals are seeded from one close, each attested to by a different session's witness. Later sessions and the kernel cannot tell which close is canonical; the double-witness pollutes the next goal's formation (the resolution rite the rite-frame demands does not exist).

severity_examples.condition: flag if any provisional-accept-then-async-verify close shape lacks a compensating action that also unwinds every DOWNSTREAM witnessed conferral (successor mint, run auto-attach, statusline retirement, reflect/compound) and not merely the Goal open/closed bit
severity_examples.intersection_justification: Orchestration alone correctly demands a compensating transaction for late verification failure -- and would consider the finding closed once the Goal bit can be flipped back. Rite alone flags a silently-reverting conferral as invalid but has no async-verify/compensation model and cannot see that the compensation exists yet is scoped too narrowly. Only the intersection sees that a transactionally-present compensation is ritually incomplete because it reverts the bit but not the witnesses the provisional accept already bound the community to -- the subject is stranded precisely because the compensating transaction stops at the entity and the rite's witnesses are downstream. Remove either half and the defect vanishes: no async-verify means no compensation scope question; no witness-downstream means the bit-flip suffices.
severity_examples.scenario: Shape (a) is adopted: /goal-met provisionally closes the Goal at session end and intercore verifies against the charter asynchronously. A session ends, the Goal is marked discharged (witnessed: kernel state flips, next-goal proposes a successor, the statusline shows the goal retired, a sibling session auto-attaches its new run to the SUCCESSOR because the parent reads as closed). Async verification then FAILS (the charter's acceptance criteria were not actually met from surfaced output). The orchestration-correct compensating transaction flips the Goal back to open. But the community already witnessed the discharge: a successor goal was minted, a run attached to it, reflect/compound artifacts were written. The compensation un-closes the entity bit but cannot un-witness the downstream conferrals -- the Goal is now a silently-reverting status holding both 'open again' (kernel) and 'was closed, has a successor and attached run' (community), a polluting liminal being with no resolution rite bound to unwind the successor and re-strand the attached run.

severity_examples.condition: flag if the strategized-collapse migration defines no per-run chain-version pin, no fencing between old-chain and new-chain cohorts, and no bound migration/resolution ceremony for in-flight runs whose declared phase is dropped from the canonical chain
severity_examples.intersection_justification: Orchestration alone flags an unversioned chain migration with two concurrent definitions and a read-consistency window -- a schema-migration hazard. Rite alone flags the in-flight cohort as separated-but-not-reincorporated stranded subjects needing a resolution ceremony -- but assumes a single chain authority and cannot articulate the concurrent-cohort read-inconsistency mechanism. Only the intersection names BOTH: the un-fenced two-cohort migration is the mechanism, and the stranded double-/no-status in-flight run with no resolution ceremony is the consequence -- and shows the goal-cadence hook mis-reads the polluted run precisely because the migration left it mid-threshold. Delete orchestration and there is no concurrent-cohort mechanism; delete rite and it is a benign per-run flag with no stranded-subject stakes.
severity_examples.scenario: Decision 5 collapses the strategized phase from DefaultChain for new runs while in-flight runs keep their chain via per-run --phases, with the transition policy explicitly undesigned. In-flight runs were cut from participation in the new goal-formation-head chain (separation happened by virtue of the chain redefinition) but are never reincorporated into it -- they finish under a chain definition the kernel is retiring. There is no fencing between the two chain cohorts and no bound migration ceremony (resolution rite). An in-flight run that a hook re-reads mid-flight can find its declared phase (strategized) no longer present in the canonical chain the hook now loads, stranding it between a phase-status the new chain does not witness and one it was never cut into -- a polluting ambiguous run that the goal-cadence Stop-hook (now reading the entity instead of regex) mis-classifies.

severity_examples.condition: flag if the mandatory successor-proposal is modeled as an optional/best-effort consumer of an unordered close event with no ordered, enforced terminal phase and no detection that the reincorporation's final witnessed step failed to bind
severity_examples.intersection_justification: Orchestration alone flags that an optional consumer cannot enforce a mandatory doctrine (its own axiom) -- an enforcement-semantics defect. Rite alone flags that a reincorporation is incomplete until its final witnessed phase binds and that phases must complete in order -- but has no event/consumer model and cannot see WHY the terminal phase is skippable. Only the intersection maps the optional-consumer mechanism onto the terminal-phase-of-the-rite and shows that the unordered best-effort event structurally lets the mandatory final witness silently not-fire, leaving a closed-yet-unfinished passage. Remove orchestration and there is no consumer-optionality mechanism; remove rite and a missed successor is a nice-to-have, not an incomplete binding status-transition.
severity_examples.scenario: Shape (c) (event-driven close: a goal-close event with registered, individually-optional, unordered consumers) is adopted, with successor-proposal as one consumer. The Goal-close event fires and durably discharges the Goal (old status cut, witnessed). But successor-proposal -- the terminal witnessed phase the mandatory doctrine ('never leave a finished goal without a proposed successor') requires -- is best-effort and, on a busy session or a consumer error, does not fire. The Goal is closed and witnessed as discharged, yet its reincorporation's final binding phase never completed: the just-finished goal sits in a margin where the successor attestation the doctrine mandates never became real, and because the consumers are unordered, reflect/compound may have fired while the mandatory successor did not -- an out-of-order, phase-incomplete rite that reads as fully closed.

severity_examples.condition: flag if interphase retirement preserves the statusline witness without an atomic cutover or single-source reconciliation, leaving a window where the daily-visible phase witness attests to a status the retired authority no longer confers and the kernel authority has already changed
severity_examples.intersection_justification: Orchestration alone flags a two-system consistency window during cutover -- a dual-write/read-consistency defect. Rite alone flags a community witness that outlives the authority that conferred it -- a hollow-status defect -- but assumes one authority and cannot articulate the cutover-window mechanism. Only the intersection connects the non-atomic two-authority cutover to the specific hazard that the preserved daily witness keeps attesting to a status no living authority confers, and that downstream hooks/sessions trust that hollow witness. Remove orchestration and there is no window (atomic swap); remove rite and a stale statusline is a cosmetic lag, not a validity defect in the status other actors act on.
severity_examples.scenario: interphase is retired as the phase authority but its statusline display (the daily-visible community witness) is preserved via a consumer story that still renders phase from the interphase file sideband. The kernel chain now owns phase (new authority), but the cutover is not atomic across the two systems: for some window, the kernel has reincorporated a run into a new phase while the interphase-fed statusline still attests to the old one. Users -- and any hook or sibling session that trusts the statusline witness -- read a status the retired authority no longer confers and the new authority has already superseded: a witnessed-but-hollow status conferred by a dead officiant.

source_domain: distributed-transaction close semantics x pre-modern rite-of-passage (the crossing that is simultaneously a fenced/idempotent/compensable transaction AND a witnessed three-phase status-rite)
success_hints: Every reported finding names BOTH a concrete transactional mechanism (a fencing token or its absence, an idempotency/replay path, a provisional-accept + async-verify + compensation shape, a per-step checkpoint vs. single open/closed bit, an optional-consumer wiring, a two-system/two-cohort consistency window) AND a concrete rite consequence (a stranded liminal subject, a missing-separation double-status, an un-witnessed or silently-reverting conferral, a phase-skip, a hollow witness outliving its authority, a polluting half-crossing with no resolution ceremony) -- and its intersection_justification demonstrates that deleting either half collapses the finding into a single-parent concern.

Distinguishes the fused target from each parent's solo territory: a pure concurrency/idempotency/compensation bug with no stranded-subject or witness-validity stakes belongs to fd-orchestration-terminal-consistency and is DECLINED here; a pure phase-order/witness/pollution defect over a crossing already assumed atomic and single-writer belongs to fd-liminal-rite-passage and is DECLINED here.

Traces each specific crossing in the doc (charter -> Goal mint, run auto-attach, Goal -> discharge terminal sequence, strategized collapse, interphase retirement, /goal-met vs Goal close, tracker subsume) through BOTH questions at once -- is it fenced/idempotent/checkpointed/compensated AND is the old status cut before the new, does it complete in order, is the new status durably witnessed, is any subject stranded, is there a resolution rite -- rather than reasoning about transactions or rites in the abstract.

Prefers findings where a mechanism the orchestration frame RECOMMENDS (retry, provisional-accept, fencing, idempotent replay) is itself what manufactures or conceals the stranded/un-witnessed subject the rite frame fears -- the sharpest intersection is a correct-transaction that produces an invalid-rite, or a valid-rite with no transactional guarantee protecting its witness.

Grounds each finding in the doc's own artifacts and decisions (the three terminal-gate shapes a/b/c, Decision 5's strategized collapse and undesigned transition policy, interphase retirement, the goal-cadence Stop-hook reading the entity, next-goal consuming the successor proposal, /goal's session-scoped Haiku evaluator vs the goal-scoped entity) rather than importing generic saga or generic-initiation examples.
task_context: Reviewing a brainstorm doc (docs/brainstorms/2026-07-18-goal-native-cycle-brainstorm.md) that redesigns the Clavain/intercore strategy->plan->execute->review cycle around goals as the top-level unit, with two pillars: (1) a goal-FORMATION ritual (comparative-advantage inter-elicitation, research-first, single-question interviews, a charter document, stakes-routed melange review, dual terminal artifact = a durable intercore Goal entity + a machine-evaluable /goal completion condition), and (2) Goal as a new first-class intercore entity (an `ic goal` noun family; goals contain runs; /goal mints the entity; runs auto-attach; goals accumulate close evidence). The doc's OPEN QUESTIONS explicitly delegate the terminal-gate SHAPE to melange, offering three: (a) two-layer ordered close (/goal's session Haiku evaluator + a kernel-gated ordered intercore close: verify-against-charter -> reflect+compound -> next-goal successor, stakes-scaled, evidence on the entity); (b) single-layer (/goal-met IS goal completion, Stop-hook cadence fires terminal steps); (c) event-driven (goal-close event, registered consumers, unordered, individually optional). Other in-scope crossings: strategized-phase collapse from DefaultChain for new runs while in-flight runs keep their chain (transition policy undesigned); interphase retirement while preserving its statusline display; tracker subsume/supersede verdicts; the goal-cadence Stop-hook reading the entity instead of regex-matching prose; next-goal consuming the successor proposal. The review goal is 'maximize verified novelty x risk surface until dry'. This fused lens investigates ONLY the seam where a status crossing must be simultaneously a fenced/idempotent/checkpointed/compensable TRANSACTION and a witnessed, ordered, non-polluting three-phase RITE -- where the mechanism that makes it transactionally correct manufactures or conceals a stranded liminal subject, or the mechanism that makes it a valid witnessed rite has no transactional guarantee protecting the witness -- the seam neither the orchestration parent nor the rite parent can see alone.
